key_insight: Chaotic elastic-turbulence dynamics can be captured even when some simulations temporarily violate the conformation-tensor positivity constraint, as long as the run remains numerically stable.
engineering_relevance: This could substantially reduce the resolution and compute cost needed for direct numerical simulation of dilute-polymer flows, making elastic-turbulence studies more accessible.
method: Simulated dilute polymer flow in a plane channel at low Reynolds number.
Compared three resolution regimes: unstable blow-up, stable-but-nonpositive, and fully positive-definite simulations.
Assessed velocity, velocity-gradient, and polymer-stretch statistics against a positive-definite reference.
evidence_signal: Intermediate-resolution runs stayed chaotic and stable despite local Tr(c)<3 violations, and their mid-plane statistics matched fully positive-definite simulations.
watch_item: Local loss of positive-definiteness is still physically unclean and lower-resolution setups can fail catastrophically below the first threshold, so stability checks remain essential.
paper_title: No need to stay positive: a practical approach to direct numerical simulations of elastic turbulence
